diagnostics.message: module.runners:resource.aws_sqs_queue_policy.build_queue_dlq_policy incorrectly targets the build queue, rather than the dead-letter queue. Reference queued_builds_dlq[0].id so the policy is applied to, and ordered after, the intended DLQ.

module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_lambda_event_source_mapping.scale_up must wait for aws_iam_role_policy.scale_up to grant its execution role SQS receive/delete/get-attributes permissions; referencing the Lambda function alone does not order this policy before mapping creation, which validates queue access.

module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_s3_object.trigger immediately invokes the syncer through S3, but has no dependency on aws_iam_role_policy.syncer. Wait for the S3 access policy before uploading the deployment trigger so the initial sync can read/write the distribution object.

When VPC subnets are configured, aws_lambda_function.syncer must wait for syncer_vpc_execution_role to attach ENI-management permissions. Both currently depend only on the role, allowing Lambda creation before its required VPC permissions exist.

When VPC subnets are configured, aws_lambda_function.webhook must wait for webhook_vpc_execution_role to attach ENI-management permissions; the shared role reference does not ensure this attachment precedes Lambda creation.

When VPC subnets are configured, aws_lambda_function.scale_up must wait for scale_up_vpc_execution_role to attach ENI-management permissions; its role reference alone does not order the attachment before Lambda creation.

When VPC subnets are configured, aws_lambda_function.scale_down must wait for scale_down_vpc_execution_role to attach ENI-management permissions; its role reference alone does not order the attachment before Lambda creation.

When the pool and VPC subnets are configured, aws_lambda_function.pool must wait for pool_vpc_execution_role to attach ENI-management permissions; sharing a role dependency does not ensure the required attachment exists before Lambda creation.
